provenance: New, hand-authored synthetic stress corpus. Written before model scoring; independent from the existing three-memory calibration/held-out fixture, but not externally sampled or independently annotated.

protocol.policyOrigin: Both policies copied unchanged from the previous three-memory evaluation. Neither policy is selected or tuned on this new corpus.
protocol.input: For each case generate two JUnit failures with identical diagnostic content and different timestamps, PIDs and source paths/positions. parseJUnit -> groupFailures -> group.signature -> embedTextsNode. Memory input is normalizeFailure(incident.symptom) only.
metrics: tokenizer truncation and identical retained-prefix probes
parser/grouping, startup, warm single-query and ranking latency
protocol.labels: Known cases intentionally share a stored incident cause; novel cases explicitly distinguish a cause absent from memory even when error codes overlap. Ground truth is authored, not proven by execution. Stress subset reported separately.
protocol.constraints: No score-based exclusions, relabeling, policy tuning, test-set tuning, human-time-saved claims, or production-accuracy claims. All first-run scores are retained. Repeats are regression checks, not fresh held-out evidence.

tailTruncationProbe.expectedObservation: When diagnostic differences fall after token 256, the model cannot observe them. Ranking equality is an information-loss finding, not a root-cause result.

timings.note: Sequential batch-of-one inference; model already initialized. CPU native runtime with existing cache, uncontrolled shared-host load. No browser, first download, network, end-to-end human workflow or time-saved measurement.

limitations: All cases and labels were authored by one evaluator, not externally sampled, independently annotated or confirmed by execution.
The 20-memory notebook and 65 probes are still small. Precision and false-accept rates describe this exact construction only.
Shared error codes can mask distinct causes. Neither exact symptoms nor cosine similarity establishes that a historical fix is applicable.
The fixed policies were originally calibrated against just three memories. No claim is made that they are calibrated for larger or different notebooks.
The lexical baseline uses full normalized text; semantic inference truncates at 256 tokens. This reflects the actual pipelines, not matched input budgets.
Top-3 ranking is now over 20 candidates and is measured before abstention, not the number of suggestions actually surfaced.
Generated JUnit exercises parser/group/model integration but is not the UI import path, browser WASM, a production report, or a real CI remediation study.
Runtime numbers are shared-host Node CPU measurements and must not be presented as browser latency or developer time saved.
